#### File: ./README.md
```
# Bundle

> **Track:** Track 1: Solving Fragmented Intelligence
> **Sponsor technology:** Zetaris (SQL data door), Meterless (H-MEM memory engine; Nightshift as the AI switchboard on the Mac), NVIDIA-hosted models (supported; not in the saved results)
> **How it was built:** Built with Claude Code. Cursor was optional for this hackathon and was not used.
> **Run with no keys:** `cp .env.example .env && npm ci && npm run dev`, then `POST /api/run` on port 5050

## 1. What Bundle does (in plain English)

New parents are owed money, benefits and safety information that is scattered across a dozen places: a tax credit on
one government site, a leave programme on another, a refund window buried in a store's help page, a crib-mattress
recall on a federal safety feed. Nobody has time to line these up, and many "free" baby offers hide a paid
membership in the fine print.

Bundle is a small team of AI helpers ("agents": programs that each do one job and hand work to the next) that, for one
family, **find, check and prepare** these things, show where every answer came from, and learn from parent feedback.
It prepares; it does not give advice. Wording is "likely eligible", never "eligible".

- A **Benefits Planner** lists likely benefits and deadlines from the baby's birth or due date.
- A **Clawback Hunter** finds money that can come back (a price drop inside a store's adjustment window, spending that a flexible-spending account could have covered).
- A **Recall Checker** compares what the family bought with government recall lists.
- A **Fine Print Court** argues over "free" offers and rejects the ones with hidden catches.
- A **Fact-Checker** sends back, or drops, any card with no source or a wrong dollar amount or date.
- When parents report a problem, a **Coach** proposes a rule, a reviewer approves it, and the next run changes because of it.

**Year-one money figure.** Our research file estimates the first year's value for a middle-class Boston family at about
$9,210, not counting paid leave. Say it as: **"estimated from our research; about $6,040 independently source-checked."**
The checked rows (federal Child Tax Credit, Massachusetts Child and Family Tax Credit, the Trump Account deposit and
Dependent Care FSA tax savings) and their sources are in [`docs/year-one-table.md`](docs/year-one-table.md); the rest
comes from `../research/research-boston-baby-benefits.html`, which cites its own sources. Amounts are estimates, not promises.

**Every family, purchase and card in the sample data is fictional.** The recalls, benefit rules and store policies
are real public facts; see [`data/README.md`](data/README.md).

The approved one-line summary of who does what: *Zetaris finds candidate matches across private and public data in
one question. Code rules make the safety decisions and show their evidence. The AI argues over fine print,
explains, and fills gaps the rules can't, and code can overrule it.*

## 2. Agents

| Agent | Responsibility | Can block or retry? |
|---|---|---|
| Orchestrator | Runs the agents side by side; one failing never stops the rest; builds a never-empty feed | Yes (keeps going, shows a banner) |
| Clawback Hunter | Finds money that can come back: FSA/HSA-eligible spend, store price-adjustment refunds, daycare for a Dependent Care FSA | Revises when sent back |
| Recall Checker | Checks purchases against live government recall feeds through Zetaris | Revises when sent back |
| Benefits Planner | Likely benefits and deadlines from birth or due date | Revises when sent back |
| Fine Print Court | Deal hunter proposes, fine-print lawyer attacks, judge rules (max 5 offers per run) | **Yes: rejects offers** |
| Fact-Checker | Every card needs a source link, correct dollars and dates | **Yes: sends back up to 2 times, then drops the card and logs it** |
| Coach | Turns "report an issue" feedback into proposed rules; a reviewer approves them into memory. **Offline (no model), the Coach does not write rules:** when 2 or more reports share a theme it proposes one of two pre-written rule sentences (`THEMES` in `server/agents/coach.ts`: auto-renewing membership, shipping fee). With a model it clusters and words the rule itself | Proposes only |
| Scout (script) | Reads 3 saved pages and proposes benefit rows; rows not written on the page are rejected | Scout's own checks (and the Fact-Checker's no-source rule) reject; the saved run uses a scripted stand-in model |

What makes this more than a chain: the agents share one memory (learned rules), the Fact-Checker can send work back
or drop it, the Court can block an offer, sources can fail and the run still finishes, and a rule learned in run 1
changes the outcome of run 2. Diagram: [`docs/architecture.md`](docs/architecture.md).

## 3. Tech stack

| Part | Technology |
|---|---|
| Server | Node 24, Express, TypeScript |
| App | React, Vite, Tailwind (mobile first, 375px) |
| Data door | **Zetaris**: one SQL layer over a Neon Postgres database and live public recall feeds |
| Memory | **Meterless H-MEM** (Meterless's open-source memory engine, copied into `vendor/hmem` under Apache-2.0 and run inside our own server) |
| AI switchboard | **Meterless Nightshift** (a Mac app; first choice for AI calls when it is running; see section 14) |
| Models | NVIDIA Nemotron models, reached through Nightshift or directly (an "OpenAI-compatible endpoint" is a standard web address AI services share). Not exercised in the saved results |
| Database | Neon Postgres via Drizzle (live mode only) |
| Built with | Claude Code (AI coding assistant) |
| Logging | One JSON line per event in `logs/run-<id>.jsonl` |

## 4. Quick start

Needs Node 24 or newer (`package.json` says `>=24`; check yours with `node -v`, get it from nodejs.org). In our clean-download rehearsal the sample run, tests, type check, build and eval also passed on Node 22.22, but 24 is the stated requirement. No GPU. **No keys for the sample run.**

### Option A: sample mode, no keys

`SAMPLE_MODE=true` (already set in `.env.example`) means the app runs from saved sample families and saved Zetaris answers, and never calls Zetaris or an AI model.

```bash
git clone <repo-url>     # download the project (use the address of this repository, on the submission branch)
cd parent-benefits/bundle
cp .env.example .env     # SAMPLE_MODE=true is already set
npm ci                   # takes about 20 seconds
npm run dev              # http://localhost:5050
```

`npm ci` prints "30 vulnerabilities" at the end. That is normal for this sample app and can be ignored. The server starts in a few seconds. The terminal will scroll with lines of JSON; that is the agents' activity log, not an error. The line "serving on port 5050" means it is ready. Open http://localhost:5050 for the app, or call the API below.

Other commands:

```bash
npm test         # unit tests, about 1.5 minutes. The one live-database test (it reseeds Neon) is skipped unless you run RUN_DB_TESTS=1 npm test
npm run check    # type check
npm run eval     # the evals (answer key); the output is very long (about 1,400 lines), so scroll to the end and look for "trapsCaught": 8, "falseAlarms": 0
npm run build && npm start   # production build
```

Heads-up: `npm test` and `npm run eval` rewrite some saved files that are tracked in git (`bundle/logs/scoreboard.json` and `bundle/output_examples/learning/*.jsonl`), so `git status` will show changes afterwards. That is expected. To undo it, run `git checkout -- bundle/logs bundle/output_examples` from the repo root.

### Option B: real keys (live mode)

Everything the app can be told is listed, with plain-English comments and safe placeholders, in
[`.env.example`](.env.example). Copy it to `.env` (git-ignored) and fill in only what you have:

1. `SAMPLE_MODE=false`.
2. Database: `DATABASE_URL` (a Neon Postgres address), then `npm run seed` to fill the benefit rules and offers.
3. Zetaris: `ZETARIS_BASE_URL`, `ZETARIS_ORG_ID`, `ZETARIS_API_KEY`.
4. AI, either or both: Nightshift on a Mac (`NIGHTSHIFT_TOKEN_FILE`, plus the model names in `.env.example`), and/or NVIDIA direct (`MODEL_API_KEY`, `MODEL_REASONING`, `MODEL_FAST`). `MODEL_PROVIDER` picks the order (`auto` is Nightshift, then NVIDIA, then offline text).

Never commit `.env`. Never run `npm run db:push`: database changes here are applied as reviewed SQL, by hand, with the
owner's OK. Mac-only steps (Nightshift, recording new Zetaris answers) are in [`docs/mac-flip-on-checklist.md`](docs/mac-flip-on-checklist.md).

### Running the live-database test (opt-in)

`server/__tests__/seed.test.ts` clears and refills Bundle's own tables in Neon, so it never runs by accident. A normal `npm test` prints "Skipping seed.test.ts..." and moves on. To run it on purpose (needs `DATABASE_URL`):

```bash
RUN_DB_TESTS=1 npm test -- seed
```

### When you have an AI key (Nightshift or NVIDIA)

Put the key in `.env` (or the private settings file the server also reads; never commit it), then run these three commands in order:

```bash
npm run model:check -- --write   # 1. asks NVIDIA which Nemotron models your key can use, saves MODEL_REASONING and MODEL_FAST, sends one tiny test message to each and prints how long it took
npm run eval:live-model          # 2. the full eval, then the learning demo, with the real model; the scoreboard's llmMode names who really answered, e.g. "nightshift:<model ids>" or "nvidia-direct:<model ids>" ("mixed:" with counts if both did), instead of "offline-fallback"
npm run examples:regen           # 3. re-runs the saved example families into output_examples/ and logs/sample/ (replays the saved Zetaris answers; add -- --live to ask Zetaris live)
```

`model:check` stops with an error if there is no key or a model does not answer. Without `--write` it only suggests the two model ids. After step 3, update the "Every saved run here is offline" note in section 8 to match, and review the diff before committing.

### Deploy (Render)

`render.yaml` in the repo root describes the web service (build `npm ci --include=dev && npm run build`, start `npm start`; `--include=dev` is needed because with `NODE_ENV=production` plain `npm ci` skips the build tools). Nothing is created until you connect the repo on render.com and pick this file.

- **Use an always-on paid instance** (not the free tier): free instances go to sleep after inactivity and take about a minute to wake, which looks broken to a judge. `render.yaml` asks for the `starter` plan.
- **Environment variables** (already in `render.yaml`): `NODE_ENV=production`, `SAMPLE_MODE=true`, `TRUST_PROXY=1`.
- **Leave out** all `ZETARIS_*` keys and `DATABASE_URL` so the host replays the saved answers (see the hosting checklist below). Optional: `FRONTEND_URL`, `REVIEWER_MODE_TOKEN`, and `MODEL_API_KEY` / `MODEL_REASONING` / `MODEL_FAST` for real model text (enter secrets in Render's dashboard; `render.yaml` marks them `sync: false`).
- Health check: `/`.

### Hosting checklist (for a public demo)

1. `SAMPLE_MODE=true`. In this mode the app is always offline (it never calls Zetaris or the model and never writes the saved answers), even if keys are present on the host. Still, leave the keys off a public host.
2. `NODE_ENV=production`. `npm start` sets it for you; if your host starts the app another way, set it yourself. In production the app trusts one proxy hop so each visitor gets their own rate limit (`TRUST_PROXY=0` turns that off).
3. `npm ci && npm run build && npm start`. Optional: `FRONTEND_URL` (the site's own address, for CORS) and `REVIEWER_MODE_TOKEN` if you want Approve to work for visitors.
4. Check it from two different networks (e.g. a laptop and a phone on mobile data): both should be able to run a sample family, and each gets its own limits.

## 5. Usage

```bash
curl -s -XPOST 'localhost:5050/api/run?wait=true' \
  -H 'content-type: application/json' \
  -d @input_examples/leo.json
```

Request (a sample family, or type your own: `{"zip":"02446","birthDate":"2026-10-10"}`; a birth date must be within the last 2 years, a due date within the next 10 months):

```json
{ "familyId": "leo" }
```

Response (abridged; full files in `output_examples/`):

```json
{
  "runId": "leo-34c1e1b4-...",
  "cards": [
    { "kind": "benefit", "title": "Federal Child Tax Credit", "amountCents": 220000, "verdict": "likely",
      "sources": [{ "label": "Federal Child Tax Credit", "url": "https://www.irs.gov/credits-deductions/individuals/child-tax-credit" }] }
  ],
  "receipt": { "moneyBackCents": 0, "likelyBenefitsCents": 364000, "deadlineCount": 2, "nextDeadline": "2027-01-06", "itemsChecked": 0 }
}
```

Without `?wait=true` the call returns `202 {runId}` right away; poll `GET /api/runs/:runId`, and read the agents' trace
at `GET /api/runs/:runId/trace`. Other routes: `GET /api/scoreboard`, `POST /api/feedback`, `GET /api/case-law`.
Money is integer cents, computed in code, never by the model.

## 6. Sample mode (honest version)

`SAMPLE_MODE=true` (the default in `.env.example`) lets you run with **no keys and no database**:

- The three families come from `data/sample/families.json` (made up).
- **Zetaris is answered from saved real responses** (`data/sample/zetaris-cache/`, 126 files, captured 2026-10-23 by running the agents live against Zetaris). Nothing is pre-written: the agents still run their queries, the fact-checks and the court. See `data/README.md`.
- **Without `MODEL_API_KEY`, the model-written parts fall back to deterministic text.** The Fine Print Court uses a plain screen (rejects offers matching a learned rule's keywords, a stated shipping/handling fee over $5 or a fee that "may apply", or fine print that says Prime/a membership is required; trace status `fallback`). Its approvals say so: "Offline screen: no flagged terms found. Not reviewed by the AI court." It does not catch a free trial that auto-renews into a paid plan until a parent-reported rule teaches it (that is the learning demo). Explanations use fixed text.
- Memory is H-MEM running locally (folder `data/hmem`, created on first run).
- The sample families run on a fixed **demo date, 2026-10-23**, so their deadlines make sense. Change it with `TODAY=YYYY-MM-DD`. A family you type in uses the real date.
- A family you type in is never saved, so it has no purchases or card data: Clawback and Recall skip their lookups (the Receipt then says "Connect your data to safety-check items", never "all clear"). Benefits and the Fine Print Court still run on the saved shared data (benefit rules, the offers table), so a typed-in family gets checked benefit cards and court-judged offers with no banner (`output_examples/custom-family.json`). Anything that was never saved in the replay cache fails safely: the failure handling shows a banner and "Not yet verified" stand-ins, which sit in their own section, outside the Receipt, and never under "Deals that passed Fine Print Court".
- `SAMPLE_MODE=true` is always offline: it never calls live Zetaris or the model and never writes `data/sample/zetaris-cache/`, whatever keys are in your environment or private settings file. To capture new live answers, turn SAMPLE_MODE off.

### Try the learning loop (2 minutes, no keys)

This is the main idea: parents' feedback becomes a rule in memory that changes the next run. Reviewer mode is **off** unless you set a code, so first:

1. In `.env` set `REVIEWER_MODE_TOKEN=demo`, then restart `npm run dev`.
2. Run the maya sample (tap "Try as guest" in the app, or `curl -s -XPOST 'localhost:5050/api/run?wait=true' -H 'content-type: application/json' -d '{"familyId":"maya"}'`). Note the **"Free newborn diaper box"** card under the deals (its id is in the response; this is the planted trap: a "free" box that turns into a paid membership).
3. Report it twice (in the app: open the card, "Report issue"; or the API, using that card's id):
   `curl -s -XPOST localhost:5050/api/feedback -H 'content-type: application/json' -d '{"familyId":"maya","cardId":"<that card id>","kind":"issue","note":"free box turned into a paid monthly membership"}'` (send it two times).
4. `curl -s localhost:5050/api/case-law` shows the proposed rule (or open "Bundle got smarter" in the app).
5. Approve it: `curl -s -XPOST localhost:5050/api/case-law/<proposal id>/approve -H 'x-reviewer-token: demo'` (in the app: "Bundle got smarter", open Reviewer mode, enter `demo`, tap "Approve rule").
6. Run maya again: the card is gone, and the run's trace (`GET /api/runs/<runId>/trace`) shows the judge blocking it and citing the new `mem-…` rule.
7. The rule lives in `data/hmem/` (git-ignored). Delete that folder to reset.

Offline, the proposal wording comes from one of two pre-written sentences (see the Coach row above). The same flow, scripted, is `npm run eval -- --learning` (writes `output_examples/learning/run1.jsonl` and `run2.jsonl`). `server/__tests__/sampleMode.test.ts` runs these exact steps.

Live mode: set `SAMPLE_MODE=false`, `DATABASE_URL`, the `ZETARIS_*` values and `MODEL_*` values, then `npm run seed`.
Secrets go only in `.env` (git-ignored). `.env.example` holds placeholders.

## 7. How failures are handled

| What fails | What happens |
|---|---|
| A Zetaris query errors or times out | One retry for one known transient error (the purchases query, errors mentioning thrift or resultset); then a saved response if one exists (logged as `fallback`); otherwise that agent is skipped, the others finish, and the feed shows a banner |
| An agent throws | The orchestrator logs `agent_failed` and continues |
| The model is unavailable | Deterministic text and a plain court screen (its approvals are labelled "Offline screen ... Not reviewed by the AI court"); logged as `fallback` |
| A claim has no source, or a wrong amount or date | Fact-Checker sends it back (max 2), then drops it and logs the drop |
| Too little to show | The feed is never empty: fixed minimums of benefits, one recall card, discounts, and two "coming soon" tiles (pre-filled applications, price-drop watching) |
| Abuse | Rate limit of 10 runs per IP per 10 minutes; at most 2 runs at once per IP and 5 at once overall; typed-in families are never saved |

## 8. Proof: logs and the scoreboard

- Every Zetaris query, memory call and agent step is one JSON line (fields: `timestamp, trace_id, agent_name, action, input_summary, output_summary, target_agent, confidence, retry_count, status`). Saved runs: `logs/sample/` (maya, leo, ava, custom-family). Live runs write `logs/run-<id>.jsonl`.
- `npm run eval` prints the scoreboard and saves `logs/scoreboard.json`. Result of `SAMPLE_MODE=true npm run eval`, saved at 2026-10-25T12:56Z (demo date 2026-10-23; it exits 0).

| Measure | Result |
|---|---|
| Planted traps caught | **8 of 8** (auto-renew offer, wrong-amount Scout row, recalled crib mattress, duplicate purchase, out-of-state family, a subtler subscription-savings trap taught by the learning demo, and two recall checks: look-alike products get no recall card; finished FDA recalls get none). `expectationFailures` is empty. |
| False alarms | **0** |
| Cards with a source | **100%** |
| Stable across 3 sample runs | yes |
| Money back found | Maya $48.99, Leo $0.00, Ava $14.58 |
| Learning demo | Run 1 approves the "free trial that auto-renews" offer; a reviewer-approved rule is stored in memory; run 2 **blocks** it and cites that rule (`mem-28`, "Reject offers whose savings depend on keeping a subscription active"; the subtle trap is the Amazon Subscribe & Save diaper discount, and the obvious free-diaper-box trap is also blocked, citing `mem-29`) |
| Who answered | `llmMode: "offline-fallback"`, Scout `fake-llm` (no real AI model) |

  **Every saved run here is offline** (`llmMode: "offline-fallback"`, Scout `fake-llm`): no real AI model was used for the scoreboard, the examples or the traces. Offline, the Fine Print Court's debate lines are "model unavailable" and the Coach picks from two pre-written rule sentences once 2 or more reports share a theme (see the Coach row in §2), so the learning demo shows the *mechanism* (feedback, then memory, then a changed outcome), not AI-written rules. A real-model run can be added with `npm run eval:live-model` once a model key is available (see "When you have an NVIDIA key" in section 4). The learning traces are in `output_examples/learning/`: `run1.jsonl`, `approve.jsonl` (the reviewer's approval: the `memory add_rule` call) and `run2.jsonl` (`memory recall_rules` returns the rule, then the judge blocks the offer and cites it).

## 10. Data and licences

See [`data/README.md`](data/README.md): each source, licence, record count, how to rebuild it, and limits. All families
and purchases are made up. No real personal data and no income in logs.

## 11. Limitations

- Sample mode replays saved Zetaris answers, so only the three sample families run fully offline.
- The saved scoreboard, examples and traces used offline fallbacks; model quality is not measured there, and the offline Coach reuses two pre-written rule sentences.
- Offline, the Fine Print Court is a plain screen, not a judgement: it catches stated fees and membership requirements, not everything.
- Benefit amounts and windows are hand-checked as of 2026-10-23 and can go stale. Poverty-guideline figures were not independently re-verified.
- Offers are one hand-checked snapshot; the Scout demo reads only 3 saved, hand-written page excerpts.
- No real bank or retailer connections; the sample purchase data is a made-up fixture. The Amazon upload is optional.
- "Likely eligible" is a screening, not a determination.
- Zetaris data-quality rules were not set up; the Fact-Checker's "no source" rule is the enforced backstop.

## 12. Pre-existing components (not built during Oct 22-27)

- **VibeCode starter template** (MIT), upstream commit 6af369a (the task notes cite a9542c2, the Firebase-era commit; we used the later guest-only HEAD). Imported in commit `b2bc3be`, then trimmed (auth, payments and chat removed). It provides the Express/React/Drizzle skeleton.
- **Meterless H-MEM reference implementation** (Apache-2.0), vendored unchanged in `vendor/hmem` (see its NOTICE).
- **Zetaris getting-started** patterns (query client shape, REST table recipe).
- **Pre-Oct-22 research and planning** (benefit research, plans).

Everything else (agents, orchestrator, Fact-Checker, court, Coach, Scout, evals, UI, seed data, sample cache) was built in the hackathon window.

## 13. Sponsor tech: what each one really does

- **Zetaris (a SQL "data door": one place to ask questions that span several scattered data sources).** Agents read their data through Zetaris and not straight from Postgres or the recall sites (`server/adapters/zetaris.ts`); a run reads the family profile through Zetaris too (`familyProfileSql` in `server/agents/savedVerdicts.ts`), falling back to our Neon database (via Drizzle, our database toolkit) if Zetaris cannot answer; feedback is stored through Drizzle in live mode, and the court's finished grades are saved to our own database by `server/agents/offerChecks.ts` (we do not write through Zetaris). The real cross-source join: **one question joins a family's private purchase list with live government recall feeds** (our Postgres `bundle_pg` x `bundle_live.cpsc_recalls` and `bundle_live.fda_food_recalls`), written in `pairsSql` in `server/agents/recall.ts`; fixed matching rules in `recallMatch.ts` then decide which pairs are real. Other reads go through registered views (`v_purchase_items`, `v_judge_offers`, `v_offer_verdicts`, `v_clawback_tx`, `v_recall_orders` and others). The objects are defined in `scripts/zetaris/register.ts` and every query is a trace line. In sample mode answers come from saved real Zetaris responses (`data/sample/zetaris-cache/`), replayed by the exact SQL text.
- **Meterless H-MEM (Meterless's open-source memory engine).** Stores the rules parents teach Bundle (with a confidence number and an append-only history log, "the ledger"); the Fine Print Court recalls them and must cite them (`server/adapters/memory.ts`, `server/agents/finePrintCourt.ts`; the engine is `vendor/hmem/`). The run also exports the ledger to `logs/ledger-<runId>.jsonl` (`server/agents/orchestrator.ts`). Each run also opens a shared "workspace" in H-MEM where agents leave notes for each other (`server/agents/workspace.ts`) and the court reuses grading "lessons" (`server/agents/newsroom.ts`); see section 14.
- **Meterless Nightshift (a Meterless Mac app we use as the AI switchboard).** First choice for every AI question when it is running on the same Mac (`server/adapters/llm.ts`, setting `MODEL_PROVIDER`). It passes the hard questions to NVIDIA Nemotron using a key kept inside Nightshift. Details and fallbacks: section 14.
- **NVIDIA:** Nemotron models, reached through Nightshift or directly with `MODEL_API_KEY` (`server/adapters/llm.ts`); everything degrades to offline text. No live model run is included in the saved scoreboard or examples.
- **Claude Code:** the AI coding assistant this project was built with. Cursor was optional for this hackathon and was not used.

## 14. Meterless honesty note

What actually runs through Meterless, and what does not. "Fallback" means the app keeps working with a plainer substitute and says so in its trace.

**Meterless H-MEM: runs in every mode, offline too.** It is a library copied into this repo and run inside our server (no Meterless service is called). It does real work today: approved rules from parent feedback are stored in it and recalled by the Fine Print Court (the `recall_hmem` trace lines), and the learning demo (`npm run eval -- --learning`) shows a rule changing the next run. Engines used: **H-MEM only**, for case law, plus the workspace notes and newsroom-loop lessons described below. **Not used: Meterless's Markovian and World Model engines.** Our AI steps are short, and Zetaris plus our saved-grades table already hold the shared facts. H-MEM's AI-based extraction and "dreaming" are also not used in a run.

**Workspace and newsroom lessons: wired into every run.** The orchestrator opens one shared workspace per run (logged as `workspace_open`), where agents post `claim`, `question`, `answer`, `correction` and `verdict` notes into H-MEM. The Fine Print Court reads earlier saved grades through Zetaris and past lessons from H-MEM, skips the AI when an offer's wording is unchanged, and an "offer-check writer" saves its finished grades to our own database (`server/agents/offerChecks.ts`). The Fact-Checker uses `checkWithCorrections`: it sends a card back with a note, the owning agent revises, and the Fact-Checker marks a lesson helpful or wrong, which raises or lowers its confidence. A whole run has a 300-second budget (`RUN_DEADLINE_SECONDS`); past it, no new checking starts and the feed still finishes. You can see all of this in a run's trace (`GET /api/runs/:runId/trace`, or the Agent Workspace panel in the app) as `recall_hmem` and workspace lines.

**What Meterless is used for, and what is not.** Used: **H-MEM** (memory) and **Nightshift** (AI routing, Mac only). **Not used:** Meterless's **Scout Intent** (its safety gatekeeper that checks for prompt injection and issues signed permission slips), **Markovian** and **World Model**. Our injection checks (text written to trick the AI) are our own code (`server/agents/finePrintRules.ts`), not a Meterless product; the Scout script (`scripts/scout.ts`) is our own page reader and only shares the name. Details: `../progress/reviews/meterless-safety-research.md`.

**Meterless Nightshift: runs only on Lyndsay's Mac.** Nightshift listens at `http://127.0.0.1:8088/v1` on that computer, so a cloud server, a hosted demo or a judge's machine cannot reach it. With `MODEL_PROVIDER=auto` the order is:

| Situation | Who answers AI questions |
|---|---|
| Mac, Nightshift running, token file readable (`NIGHTSHIFT_TOKEN_FILE`) | **Nightshift**, which forwards to NVIDIA Nemotron. Each call is traced with the provider and model that answered. |
| Nightshift missing or a call to it fails, and `MODEL_API_KEY`, `MODEL_REASONING` and `MODEL_FAST` are set | **NVIDIA direct** (`integrate.api.nvidia.com`). |
| Neither is available, `MODEL_PROVIDER=offline`, `SAMPLE_MODE=true` (unless `LIVE_MODEL=true`), or the 300-second run limit has passed | **Offline deterministic text**: fixed sentences, and a plain rule-based screen instead of the AI court ("Offline screen: ... Not reviewed by the AI court"). |

What the saved evidence shows: the committed scoreboard, `output_examples/` and `logs/sample/` were all produced **offline** (`llmMode: "offline-fallback"`); none of it passed through Nightshift or NVIDIA. Zetaris replays were recorded with the AI off on purpose. A Mac check on Oct 24 reached Nemotron through Nightshift (see `../progress/handoffs/HANDOFF-cloud.md`), and the full-AI scoreboard run is a Mac step (`npm run eval:live-model`, see `docs/mac-flip-on-checklist.md`). Until that is run and its output saved, do not read any saved result here as showing a live model. **To be recorded on the Mac (not done yet):** a saved full-AI run through Nightshift; this paragraph will be updated once that output exists. <!-- TODO W6: live Nightshift run, Mac step -->

Even with a live model, money amounts and recall decisions are computed by code rules, not by the AI, and code can overrule the AI.

## 15. Streaming and the saved feed

The app shows a saved feed instantly and updates it as the agents finish, with a status pill for each agent.

- `GET /api/runs/:runId/events` streams the run as server-sent events (a one-way, long-open web connection): `agent_status`, `card_ready`, `card_updated`, `card_removed`, then `end` (`server/routes/streamRoutes.ts`).
- Parents only ever receive events passed through the parent whitelist: cards are copied through the same safe-fields filter as everywhere else, only known agent names and their states are sent, and free-text labels and removal reasons stay owner-only.
- If the stream is missing or breaks, the app quietly falls back to asking `GET /api/runs/:runId` once a second (`client/src/lib/stream.ts`, `client/src/lib/poll.ts`). You can also poll `GET /api/runs/:runId/trace` by hand to watch the agents' steps.

**Forget my items.** The Extras tab has a "Forget my items" button (with a plain-English confirm step) that deletes the products saved from a family's photos (`POST /api/photo/forget`).

## 16. Try it yourself

Needs Node 24 or newer (it also worked on Node 22.22 in testing). No keys, no database. First download the project (`git clone <repo-url>`, then `cd parent-benefits`; the commands below assume you are in that top folder):

```bash
cd bundle
cp .env.example .env     # SAMPLE_MODE=true is already set
npm ci                              # about 20 seconds
SAMPLE_MODE=true npm run dev        # starts on http://localhost:5050 (scrolling JSON lines are the activity log, not errors)
```

In a second terminal:

```bash
curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}\n' localhost:5050/    # 200 means the app is up
curl -s -XPOST 'localhost:5050/api/run?wait=true' -H 'content-type: application/json' -d '{"familyId":"leo"}'
```

Open http://localhost:5050 and tap "Try a sample family" (made-up data). The finished list appears on its own; there is no separate "run" button. Open the Deals tab, tap a card, then "How we checked", and use "Your feed" to go back. Stop the server with Ctrl+C. Run the checks with `SAMPLE_MODE=true npm test` (about 1.5 minutes) and `npm run check`. After tests or eval, undo the rewritten saved files with `git checkout -- bundle/logs bundle/output_examples` from the repo root. Never run `npm run db:push`.

import { Switch, Route } from "wouter";
import { QueryClientProvider } from "@tanstack/react-query";
import { Component, ErrorInfo, ReactNode } from "react";
import { queryClient } from "./lib/queryClient";
import { Toaster } from "@/components/ui/toaster";
import { TooltipProvider } from "@/components/ui/tooltip";
import Start from "@/pages/Start";
import Feed from "@/pages/Feed";
import CardDetail from "@/pages/CardDetail";
import Smarter from "@/pages/Smarter";
import NotFound from "@/pages/not-found";
import TesterGate from "@/components/gate/TesterGate";

class ErrorBoundary extends Component<
  { children: ReactNode },
  { hasError: boolean }
> {
  constructor(props: { children: ReactNode }) {
    super(props);
    this.state = { hasError: false };
  }

  static getDerivedStateFromError(_: Error) {
    return { hasError: true };
  }

  componentDidCatch(error: Error, errorInfo: ErrorInfo) {
    console.error("Error caught by boundary:", error, errorInfo);
  }

  render() {
    if (this.state.hasError) {
      return (
        <div className="min-h-screen flex items-center justify-center bg-cream px-4">
          <div className="text-center">
            <h1 className="text-2xl font-extrabold mb-4 text-ink">Something went wrong</h1>
            <button
              className="min-h-[48px] bg-ink text-cream px-5 rounded-2xl font-bold"
              onClick={() => this.setState({ hasError: false })}
            >
              Try again
            </button>
          </div>
        </div>
      );
    }

    return this.props.children;
  }
}

function Router() {
  return (
    <Switch>
      <Route path="/" component={Start} />
      <Route path="/feed/:runId">{(p) => <Feed key={p.runId} />}</Route>
      <Route path="/card/:id" component={CardDetail} />
      <Route path="/smarter" component={Smarter} />
      <Route component={NotFound} />
    </Switch>
  );
}

function App() {
  return (
    <ErrorBoundary>
      <QueryClientProvider client={queryClient}>
        <TooltipProvider>
          <TesterGate>
            <Router />
          </TesterGate>
          <Toaster />
        </TooltipProvider>
      </QueryClientProvider>
    </ErrorBoundary>
  );
}

export default App;

```

// Shared set-up for the V2 acceptance tests. Not a test file itself (no ".test" in the name).
// Everything here uses the fictional sample family Maya (born 2026-10-03, ZIP 02139, demo date 2026-10-23 = 20 days old).
import React from 'react';
import { render, screen, within, fireEvent } from '@testing-library/react';
import { Router, Route } from 'wouter';
import { memoryLocation } from 'wouter/memory-location';
import VersionB from '@/pages/tabs/VersionB';
import Feed from '@/pages/Feed';
import { sampleRun } from '@/test-support/sampleRuns';
import type { SavedRun } from '@/lib/bundle';

/** The onboarding answer codes the tests expect the app to send and keep.
 *  Q4 part 1 ("Who's raising this baby?") -> household; part 2 (one row per parent) -> parent1Work / parent2Work. Q5 -> insurance. */

export const WORK = { paycheck: 'paycheck', selfEmployed: 'self_employed', notWorking: 'not_working' } as const;
export const INSURANCE = { job: 'job', marketplace: 'marketplace', medicaid: 'medicaid', tricare: 'tricare', skip: 'none_or_not_sure' } as const;

  return {
    ...run,
    familyId: over.familyId ?? run.familyId,
    family: { ...run.family!, zip: '02139', household: HOUSEHOLD.two, parent1Work: WORK.paycheck, parent2Work: WORK.paycheck, insurance: INSURANCE.job, ...(over.family ?? {}) } as SavedRun['family'],
  };
}

}

export function showVersionB(run: SavedRun) {

  const loc = memoryLocation({ path: `/feed/${run.runId}`, record: true });
  render(<Router hook={loc.hook}><VersionB run={run} owner={false} /></Router>);
  return loc;
}

/** A tab in the bottom bar, by its visible name. */
export const tab = (name: string) =>
  within(screen.getByRole('navigation', { name: 'Main' })).getByRole('button', { name: new RegExp(`^${name}`) });

export const goTab = (name: string) => fireEvent.click(tab(name));

/** The family chip in the header: a button that opens the family menu (Switch family, Your plan and saved answers). */
export const chipButton = () => screen.getByRole('button', { name: /^Family menu/ });

/** Opens the Account screen the way a parent does: tap the family chip, then "Your plan and saved answers". */
export function openAccount() {
  fireEvent.click(chipButton());
  fireEvent.click(within(screen.getByRole('menu', { name: /Family menu/i })).getByRole('menuitem', { name: /Your plan and saved answers/ }));
}

export type FakeRoute = [RegExp, (init: RequestInit | undefined, url: string) => unknown];

/** Fake server: answers each request whose URL matches a pattern; anything else gets a 404. Returns the jest mock. */
export function fakeServer(routes: FakeRoute[]) {
  const mock = jest.fn(async (url: string, init?: RequestInit) => {
    const hit = routes.find(([re]) => re.test(String(url)));
    if (!hit) return { ok: false, status: 404, json: async () => ({ error: 'not found' }) };
    const body = hit[1](init, String(url));
    return { ok: true, status: 200, json: async () => body };
  });
  (global as any).fetch = mock;
  return mock;
}

/** Calls the fake server received for a URL pattern, with parsed JSON bodies. */
export const callsTo = (mock: jest.Mock, re: RegExp) =>
  mock.mock.calls
    .filter(([u]) => re.test(String(u)))
    .map(([u, init]) => ({ url: String(u), method: (init as RequestInit | undefined)?.method ?? 'GET', body: (init as RequestInit | undefined)?.body ? JSON.parse(String((init as RequestInit).body)) : undefined }));

/** Dollars shown in an element, e.g. "$3,688.99 still to claim" -> 3688.99. */
export const dollars = (el: HTMLElement) => Number((el.textContent!.match(/\$([\d,]+(?:\.\d\d)?)/) ?? ['', 'NaN'])[1].replace(/,/g, ''));

/** A card's one-tap control by name, whether the app draws it as a button or a checkbox. */
export function control(card: HTMLElement, name: RegExp): HTMLElement {
  const c = within(card).queryByRole('button', { name }) ?? within(card).queryByRole('checkbox', { name });
  if (!c) throw new Error(`No "${name}" button inside the card "${card.getAttribute('aria-label')}"`);
  return c;
}

/** A stand-in for the browser's live-update connection (EventSource), so a test can send the run's progress messages. */
export class FakeES {
  static last: FakeES | null = null;
  listeners: Record<string, ((e: { data: string }) => void)[]> = {};
  onerror: (() => void) | null = null;
  onmessage: ((e: { data: string }) => void) | null = null;
  closed = false;
  constructor(public url: string) { FakeES.last = this; }
  addEventListener(t: string, fn: (e: { data: string }) => void) { (this.listeners[t] ||= []).push(fn); }
  close() { this.closed = true; }
  emit(type: string, payload: unknown) { for (const fn of this.listeners[type] ?? []) fn({ data: JSON.stringify(payload) }); }
}

/** Opens the "We're checking for you" screen for a run; the fake server answers the run's status with `status`. */
export function mountFeed(runId: string, status: Record<string, unknown>, extra: FakeRoute[] = []) {
  (global as any).EventSource = FakeES;
  FakeES.last = null;
  window.scrollTo = jest.fn() as unknown as typeof window.scrollTo;
  const server = fakeServer([
    [/\/agent-log|\/trace/, () => []],
    [new RegExp(`/api/runs/${runId}$`), () => status],
    ...extra,
  ]);
  const { hook } = memoryLocation({ path: `/feed/${runId}` });
  render(<Router hook={hook}><Route path="/feed/:runId" component={Feed} /></Router>);
  return server;
}

/** The checking screen's lines that are on screen right now (not the "Getting started…" placeholder). */
const shownLines = () => {
  const box = screen.queryByTestId('parent-steps');
  return box ? within(box).queryAllByRole('listitem').filter((li) => !/Getting started/.test(li.textContent ?? '')) : [];
};
const tick = (ms: number) => act(async () => { jest.advanceTimersByTime(ms); });

describe('S1b: the checking screen is honest and unhurried', () => {
  // S1 — "For a two-parent home where one parent is 'Not working right now', the checking screen has NO Dependent Care FSA
  // (or daycare tax savings) line. Lines appear one at a time and stay on screen. Only after the last line does
  // 'We found $X for your family. View my results' appear, and nothing moves on by itself: results show only after the tap."
  it('two parents, one not working: no Dependent Care FSA line, lines appear one by one, results wait for "View my results"', async () => {
    jest.useFakeTimers();
    const base = mayaRun();
    const family = { ...base.family, household: HOUSEHOLD.two, parent1Work: WORK.paycheck, parent2Work: WORK.notWorking, insurance: INSURANCE.job };
    const total = base.result.receipt.moneyBackCents + base.result.receipt.likelyBenefitsCents;
    mountFeed(base.runId, {
      runId: base.runId, familyId: 'maya', status: 'done', startedAt: new Date().toISOString(), family, today: base.today,
      demoDate: true, result: base.result, error: null, progress: [], owner: false,
    });
    await tick(0);
    expect(FakeES.last).toBeTruthy();
    // The run's agents report in and the stream ends at once: the server is fast, the screen should not be.
    act(() => {
      for (const [seq, agent] of ['benefits', 'court', 'fact_checker'].entries()) {
        FakeES.last!.emit('agent_status', { type: 'agent_status', agent, state: 'done', seq: seq + 1 });
      }
      FakeES.last!.emit('end', {});
    });

    // Wait (in small steps) for the first line, then check it is alone
    for (let i = 0; i < 30 && shownLines().length === 0; i++) await tick(100);
    expect(shownLines()).toHaveLength(1);
    expect(screen.queryByRole('button', { name: /View my results/ })).toBeNull();

    // About 1.2–1.5 seconds later, the second line joins it (the first stays)
    await tick(1500);
    expect(shownLines()).toHaveLength(2);

    // Let every timer run: all lines are there, the reveal card waits, and nothing moved on by itself
    await tick(60_000);
    const steps = screen.getByTestId('parent-steps');
    expect(within(steps).getByText(/State and federal family benefits/)).toBeTruthy();
    expect(within(steps).getByText(/Insurance deadline to add your baby/)).toBeTruthy();
    expect(within(steps).getByText(/Free registry gifts and welcome boxes/)).toBeTruthy();
    expect(within(steps).getByText(/Every result double-checked against its official source/)).toBeTruthy();
    expect(document.body.textContent).not.toMatch(/Dependent Care FSA/);
    expect(document.body.textContent).not.toMatch(/Daycare tax savings/i);
    const reveal = screen.getByRole('button', { name: /View my results/ });
    expect(screen.getByText(new RegExp(`We found \\${fmtUsdShort(total)} for your family`))).toBeTruthy();
    expect(screen.queryByRole('navigation', { name: 'Main' })).toBeNull();

    fireEvent.click(reveal);
    await tick(0);
    expect(screen.getByRole('navigation', { name: 'Main' })).toBeTruthy();
  });
});

describe('S1c: the insurance countdown pill follows the insurance answer', () => {

  it('job-based insurance shows "30 days from birth to add baby" and "Check your plan"', () => {

// Story 3: Money buckets on Home (plans/v2-feedback-response.md, "Money buckets, in detail" + section 4).
import { screen, cleanup, within } from '@testing-library/react';
import { fmtUsdShort } from '@/lib/bundle';

afterEach(() => { cleanup(); try { sessionStorage.clear(); localStorage.clear(); } catch { /* ignore */ } });

const bucket = (name: string) => screen.getByRole('region', { name });

describe('S3: Home splits the money into three buckets', () => {
  // S3 — "Home shows 'Money back now', 'At tax time' and 'Paid family leave' with the run's real amounts; tax-time money
  // says 'when you file your 2026 taxes (spring 2027)' for a 2026 baby; the Trump Account is labelled as going into the
  // baby's account; paid leave says 'up to $1,230 a week for 12 weeks'."
  it('Maya (born 2026): real amounts in each bucket, spring 2027, Trump Account in its own baby-savings box', () => {
    const run = mayaRun();
    showVersionB(run);
    const cards = run.result.cards;
    const sum = (re: RegExp) => cards.filter((c) => re.test(c.id) && (c.verdict === 'verified' || c.verdict === 'likely')).reduce((a, c) => a + (c.amountCents ?? 0), 0);

    const now = bucket('Money back now');
    expect(within(now).getByText(fmtUsdShort(sum(/^clawback-(fsa|price)-/)))).toBeTruthy(); // $48.99 for Maya

    const tax = bucket('At tax time');
    expect(within(tax).getByText(fmtUsdShort(sum(/^benefit-(federal_child_tax_credit|ma_child_tax_credit)$/)))).toBeTruthy(); // $2,640
    expect(within(tax).getByText(/when you file your 2026 taxes \(spring 2027\)/i)).toBeTruthy();
    // Oct 26 (Lyndsay): the Trump Account is not a tax credit, so it has its own "baby's savings account" box.
    expect(within(tax).queryByText(/Trump Account/)).toBeNull();
    const savings = bucket('Your baby\'s savings account');
    expect(within(savings).getByText(/Trump Account/)).toBeTruthy();
    expect(within(savings).getByText(fmtUsdShort(sum(/^benefit-trump_account$/)))).toBeTruthy(); // $1,000
    expect(within(savings).getByText(/account in your baby[’']s name/i)).toBeTruthy();

    const leave = bucket('Paid family leave');
    expect(within(leave).getByText(/up to \$1,230 a week for 12 weeks/)).toBeTruthy();
  });

  // S3 — "The tax year is worked out from the date (a baby due in 2027 means spring 2028), and 'Money back now' with no
  // receipts says 'Add a receipt to find money back', never '$0'."
  it('a baby due in 2027 says spring 2028, and an empty "Money back now" asks for a receipt instead of $0', () => {
    showVersionB(leoRun({ dueDate: '2027-01-15' }));
    expect(within(bucket('At tax time')).getByText(/2027 taxes \(spring 2028\)/i)).toBeTruthy();
    const now = bucket('Money back now');
    expect(within(now).getByText(/Add a receipt to find money back/)).toBeTruthy();
    expect(now.textContent).not.toMatch(/\$0\b/);
  });
});

// Story 4: One-tap completion, honest "Not relevant" and quick wins (plans/v2-build-plan.md, section 1 R6, lane B, section 5).
import { screen, cleanup, fireEvent, within, waitFor } from '@testing-library/react';
import { fakeServer, callsTo, mayaRun, showVersionB, goTab, dollars, control } from './helpers';

afterEach(() => { cleanup(); try { sessionStorage.clear(); localStorage.clear(); } catch { /* ignore */ } });

/** A closed drawer on the current tab, "Claimed" or "Dismissed" (opened first if it starts folded). */
function drawer(name: 'Claimed' | 'Dismissed'): HTMLElement {
  const re = name === 'Claimed' ? /^(show )?claimed(?! so far)/i : /^(show )?dismissed/i;
  const toggle = screen.queryAllByRole('button', { name: re }).find((b) => b.hasAttribute('aria-expanded'));
  if (toggle && toggle.getAttribute('aria-expanded') === 'false') fireEvent.click(toggle);
  return screen.getByRole('region', { name: name === 'Claimed' ? /^claimed(?! so far)/i : /^dismissed/i });
}
/** True when a card sits inside either drawer. */
const inDrawer = (el: HTMLElement) => { for (let n = el.parentElement; n; n = n.parentElement) if ((n.getAttribute('role') === 'region' || n.tagName === 'SECTION') && /^(claimed(?! so far)|dismissed)/i.test(n.getAttribute('aria-label') ?? '')) return true; return false; };
/** Cards with this name that are still in the main list (not in a drawer). */
const inMainList = (name: RegExp) => screen.queryAllByRole('article', { name }).filter((a) => !inDrawer(a));

/** The three money numbers on Home: "Still to claim", "Claimed so far" and the big headline total. */
function homeNumbers() {
  goTab('Home');
  return {
    still: dollars(screen.getByTestId('still-to-claim')),
    claimed: dollars(screen.getByTestId('claimed-so-far')),
    headline: dollars(screen.getByTestId('home-total-amount')),
  };
}

describe('S4: "I got this" moves the card to the Claimed drawer', () => {
  // S4 — "Tapping 'I got this' moves the card into the 'Claimed' drawer and moves its money from 'Still to claim'
  // to 'Claimed so far'."
  it('"I got this" puts the card in "Claimed" and moves its $1,000 from Still to claim to Claimed so far', () => {
    fakeServer([[/\/api\/feedback$/, () => ({ ok: true, proposals: [] })]]);
    showVersionB(mayaRun());
    expect(screen.getByTestId('still-to-claim').textContent).toMatch(/Still to claim/i);
    expect(screen.getByTestId('claimed-so-far').textContent).toMatch(/Claimed so far/i);
    const before = homeNumbers();

    goTab('Savings');
    const trump = screen.getByRole('article', { name: /Trump Account/ });
    fireEvent.click(control(trump, /I got this/i));
    expect(inMainList(/Trump Account/)).toHaveLength(0);
    expect(within(drawer('Claimed')).getByRole('article', { name: /Trump Account/ })).toBeTruthy();

    const after = homeNumbers();
    expect(after.still).toBeCloseTo(before.still - 1000, 2);
    expect(after.claimed).toBeCloseTo(before.claimed + 1000, 2);
  });
});

describe('S4: "Not relevant" lowers the money numbers and can be undone', () => {
  // S4 (R6) — "Tapping 'Not relevant' takes the card's amount off 'Still to claim' and off the big headline number on Home
  // at once, leaves 'Claimed so far' alone, moves the card to a closed 'Dismissed' drawer and tells the Coach
  // (feedback kind 'not_relevant'). 'Undo' puts the card and all three numbers back."
  it('"Not relevant" moves the card to "Dismissed", lowers Still to claim and the headline, and Undo restores all three', async () => {
    const server = fakeServer([[/\/api\/feedback$/, () => ({ ok: true, proposals: [] })]]);
    showVersionB(mayaRun());
    const before = homeNumbers();

    goTab('Taxes');
    const ma = screen.getByRole('article', { name: /Massachusetts Child and Family Tax Credit/ });
    fireEvent.click(control(ma, /Not relevant/i));
    expect(inMainList(/Massachusetts Child and Family Tax Credit/)).toHaveLength(0);
    expect(within(drawer('Dismissed')).getByRole('article', { name: /Massachusetts Child and Family Tax Credit/ })).toBeTruthy();
    await waitFor(() => expect(callsTo(server, /\/api\/feedback$/).map((c) => c.body)).toContainEqual(expect.objectContaining({ familyId: 'maya', cardId: 'benefit-ma_child_tax_credit', kind: 'not_relevant' })));

    const after = homeNumbers();
    expect(after.still).toBeCloseTo(before.still - 440, 2);
    expect(after.claimed).toBeCloseTo(before.claimed, 2);
    expect(after.headline).toBeCloseTo(before.headline - 440, 2);

    // Undo: from the instant Undo or from inside the Dismissed drawer
    goTab('Taxes');
    const undo = screen.queryAllByRole('button', { name: /Undo/i })[0] ?? within(drawer('Dismissed')).getByRole('button', { name: /Undo/i });
    fireEvent.click(undo);
    expect(inMainList(/Massachusetts Child and Family Tax Credit/)).toHaveLength(1);
    const undone = homeNumbers();
    expect(undone.still).toBeCloseTo(before.still, 2);
    expect(undone.claimed).toBeCloseTo(before.claimed, 2);
    expect(undone.headline).toBeCloseTo(before.headline, 2);
  });
});

describe('S4: Quick wins filter', () => {
  // S4 — "The 'Quick wins' filter shows only cards that take under 5 minutes, each with its time estimate; longer jobs
  // like adding baby to insurance (about 15 min) are hidden."
  it('shows only cards under 5 minutes', () => {
    showVersionB(mayaRun());
    fireEvent.click(screen.getByRole('button', { name: /Quick wins/i }));
    const list = screen.getByRole('region', { name: /Quick wins/i });
    const cards = within(list).getAllByRole('article');
    expect(cards.length).toBeGreaterThan(0);
    for (const c of cards) {
      const m = c.textContent!.match(/(\d+)\s*min/);
      expect(m).not.toBeNull();
      expect(Number(m![1])).toBeLessThan(5);
    }
    expect(within(list).queryByRole('article', { name: /Add your baby to health insurance/ })).toBeNull();
  });
});

describe('S5: live offer search', () => {
  /** A request that stays unanswered until the test answers it (or fails it). */
  function deferred() {
    let resolve!: (v: unknown) => void; let reject!: (e: unknown) => void;
    const promise = new Promise((res, rej) => { resolve = res; reject = rej; });
    return { promise, resolve, reject };
  }
  /** Fake server where the live offer search answers only when the test says so; everything else is "not found". */
  function serverWithPendingSearch() {
    const search = deferred();
    const mock = jest.fn((url: string) => {
      if (/offer-search/i.test(String(url))) {
        return search.promise.then((body) => ({ ok: true, status: 200, json: async () => body }));
      }
      return Promise.resolve({ ok: false, status: 404, json: async () => ({ error: 'not found' }) });
    });
    (global as any).fetch = mock;
    return { mock, search };
  }
  const SAVED_OFFER = /Free newborn diaper box/; // a saved, already-graded offer from Maya's sample run
  /** No spinner or status line is left saying "Searching". */
  const nothingStillSearching = () => {
    for (const el of [...screen.queryAllByRole('progressbar'), ...screen.queryAllByRole('status')]) expect(el.textContent ?? '').not.toMatch(/Searching/i);
    expect(screen.queryByText(/Searching 14 trusted baby-offer sites/)).toBeNull();
  };

  const live = {
    id: 'live-huggies-1', kind: 'discount', title: 'Free Huggies newborn sample pack', body: 'Free sample pack of newborn diapers and wipes. No purchase needed.',
    amountCents: 2500, deadline: null, verdict: 'verified', sources: [{ label: 'Huggies', url: 'https://www.huggies.com/en-us/offers' }], traceId: 't-live-1',
    foundOn: '2026-10-25', isNew: true,
    valueScore: { trueValueCents: 2500, effortLevel: 'low', effortMinutesEstimate: { min: 3, max: 5 }, stepsCount: 2, payoutWaitDays: null, timeLabel: 'right away', catchTypes: [], worthYourTime: true, reasons: ['Free, no purchase needed'] },
  };

  afterEach(() => { jest.useRealTimers(); });

  // S5 (R3) — "Opening Deals shows the saved, already-graded offers at once, while the live search of the trusted
  // baby-offer sites runs in the background ('Searching 14 trusted baby-offer sites…'). When it answers, new offers
  // slide in with 'New · found today' and their grade (the Value Score from the fine-print court)."
  it('saved offers show before the search answers; new offers then show "New · found today" and a grade', async () => {
    const { mock, search } = serverWithPendingSearch();
    showVersionB(mayaRun());
    goTab('Deals');

    await waitFor(() => expect(mock.mock.calls.filter(([u]) => /offer-search/i.test(String(u))).length).toBeGreaterThan(0));
    // the search has not answered yet: saved offers are already on screen
    expect(screen.getByRole('article', { name: SAVED_OFFER })).toBeTruthy();
    expect(screen.getByText(/Searching 14 trusted baby-offer sites/)).toBeTruthy();
    expect(screen.queryByRole('article', { name: /Free Huggies newborn sample pack/ })).toBeNull();

    await act(async () => { search.resolve({ mode: 'live', sitesSearched: 14, searchedOn: '2026-10-25', cards: [live] }); });
    const card = await screen.findByRole('article', { name: /Free Huggies newborn sample pack/ });
    expect(within(card).getByText(/New\s*·\s*found today/)).toBeTruthy();
    expect(within(card).getByText(/True value \$25/)).toBeTruthy();
    expect(screen.getByRole('article', { name: SAVED_OFFER })).toBeTruthy();
  });

  // S5 (R3) — "If the live search fails (error or no internet), the line changes to 'No new offers right now. Showing your
  // checked offers.' The saved offers stay, no spinner is left running and no error appears."
  it('a failed search shows "No new offers right now", keeps the saved offers and leaves nothing "Searching"', async () => {
    const { mock, search } = serverWithPendingSearch();
    showVersionB(mayaRun());
    goTab('Deals');
    await waitFor(() => expect(mock.mock.calls.filter(([u]) => /offer-search/i.test(String(u))).length).toBeGreaterThan(0));

    await act(async () => { search.reject(new TypeError('Failed to fetch')); });
    expect(await screen.findByText(/No new offers right now/)).toBeTruthy();
    expect(screen.getByRole('article', { name: SAVED_OFFER })).toBeTruthy();
    nothingStillSearching();
    expect(screen.queryByRole('alert')).toBeNull();
  });

  // S5 (R3) — "The live search gives up after 10 seconds and quietly keeps the saved offers, with the same
  // 'No new offers right now' line."
  it('a search that never answers gives up after 10 seconds with "No new offers right now"', async () => {
    jest.useFakeTimers();
    const { mock } = serverWithPendingSearch(); // never answered
    showVersionB(mayaRun());
    goTab('Deals');
    await act(async () => { await Promise.resolve(); });
    expect(mock.mock.calls.filter(([u]) => /offer-search/i.test(String(u))).length).toBeGreaterThan(0);
    expect(screen.getByRole('article', { name: SAVED_OFFER })).toBeTruthy();

    await act(async () => { jest.advanceTimersByTime(10_500); await Promise.resolve(); });
    await act(async () => { await Promise.resolve(); });
    expect(screen.getByText(/No new offers right now/)).toBeTruthy();
    expect(screen.getByRole('article', { name: SAVED_OFFER })).toBeTruthy();
    nothingStillSearching();
  });
});

/** Opens the "Switch family" menu on the Account screen and picks a family by name. */
function switchFamily(name: RegExp) {
  const page = screen.getByRole('region', { name: 'Account' });
  fireEvent.click(within(page).getByRole('button', { name: /Switch family/i }));
  const item = within(page).queryAllByRole('menuitemradio', { name })[0];
  if (!item) throw new Error(`No "${name}" choice in the Switch family menu`);
  fireEvent.click(item);
}

/** Fake server reply for GET /api/families/<id>…: the saved family plus its last finished run, in several common shapes. */
function familyReply(run: ReturnType<typeof mayaRun>) {
  const status = { runId: run.runId, familyId: run.familyId, status: 'done', startedAt: '2026-10-23T12:00:00.000Z', family: run.family, today: run.today, demoDate: run.demoDate, result: run.result, error: null };
  return { ...status, id: run.familyId, family: { id: run.familyId, ...run.family }, run: status, lastRun: status, latestRun: status };
}

    );
    goTab('Deals');
    const offer = screen.getByRole('article', { name: /Free newborn diaper box/ });
    const open = within(offer).queryAllByRole('link').find((a) => /\/card\//.test(a.getAttribute('href') ?? ''));
    if (!open) throw new Error('No link to the card detail page inside the offer card');
    setScroll(640); // the parent has scrolled down the Deals tab
    fireEvent.click(open);
    setScroll(0); // the detail page opens at the top
    expect(loc.history?.at(-1)).toMatch(/^\/card\//);

    const back = await screen.findByRole('link', { name: /Back|Your feed/ });
    fireEvent.click(back);
    await waitFor(() => expect(screen.getByRole('navigation', { name: 'Main' })).toBeTruthy());
    expect(tab('Deals').getAttribute('aria-current')).toBe('page');
    expect(tab('Home').getAttribute('aria-current')).not.toBe('page');
    // back at the same spot: window.scrollTo(0, 640) or window.scrollTo({ top: 640 })
    await waitFor(() => expect(scrollTo.mock.calls.some((a) => a[1] === 640 || (a[0] && typeof a[0] === 'object' && a[0].top === 640))).toBe(true));
  });
});

import { useEffect, type MouseEvent, type ReactNode } from 'react';
import { Link } from 'wouter';

/** Pages visited in this tab (newest last), so a "‹ Back" link can step back in history instead of stacking a new entry. */
const visited: string[] = [];
const samePath = (a: string, b: string) => { try { return decodeURIComponent(a) === decodeURIComponent(b); } catch { return a === b; } };
/** Exported for tests. When the page before this one is the link's target, go back (pressing the browser's Back then behaves as expected). */
export function backClick(e: MouseEvent, href: string): void {
  if (e.metaKey || e.ctrlKey || e.shiftKey || e.button !== 0) return;
  if (visited.length >= 2 && samePath(visited[visited.length - 2], href)) {
    e.preventDefault();
    visited.pop();
    window.history.back();
  }
}

interface Props {
  chip?: string | null;
  /** Replaces the plain chip with a control (Version B's family chip menu). */
  chipSlot?: ReactNode;
  children: ReactNode;
  back?: { href: string; label: string };
  /** A control at the right end of the header (Version B puts the "+" photo button here, so it is on every tab). */
  action?: ReactNode;
  /** Pinned to the bottom of the screen (the Version B tab bar). The page leaves room so it never covers content. */
  footer?: ReactNode;
}

/** Phone-width page frame: "bundle." wordmark, optional family chip, 16px side padding. */
export default function AppShell({ chip, chipSlot, children, back, action, footer }: Props) {
  useEffect(() => { visited.push(window.location.pathname); if (visited.length > 20) visited.shift(); }, []);
  return (
    <div className="min-h-[100dvh] bg-cream text-ink">
      <div className={`mx-auto w-full max-w-[480px] px-4 pt-5 ${footer ? 'pb-32' : 'pb-16'}`}>
        <header className="relative flex min-h-[44px] items-center justify-between gap-3">
          <Link href="/" className="text-[24px] font-extrabold tracking-[-0.03em] text-ink" aria-label="Bundle home">
            bundle<span className="text-coral">.</span>
          </Link>
          <div className="flex min-w-0 items-center gap-2">
            {chipSlot ?? (chip && (
              <span className="truncate rounded-full border border-line bg-paper px-3 py-1 text-[13px] font-semibold text-ink-2">{chip}</span>
            ))}
            {action}
          </div>
        </header>
        {back && (
          <Link href={back.href} onClick={(e) => backClick(e, back.href)} className="-ml-1 mt-2 inline-flex min-h-[44px] items-center gap-1 px-1 text-[15px] font-bold text-ink-2 hover:text-ink">
            <span aria-hidden="true">‹</span> {back.label}
          </Link>
        )}
        <main>{children}</main>
      </div>
      {footer}
    </div>
  );
}

import { useId, useRef, useState, type ChangeEvent } from 'react';

import { checkPickedFile, preparePhoto } from '@/lib/photoPrep';
import { sendAudit, verdictLabel } from '@/lib/offers';

type Source = 'paste' | 'screenshot';
type Phase = { kind: 'form' } | { kind: 'sending' } | { kind: 'done'; reply: AuditReply; store: string; offer: string } | { kind: 'problem'; message: string };

const pill: Record<AuditReply['verdict'], string> = {
  approve: 'bg-[#E3F3EA] text-[#17643F]',
  approve_with_catch: 'bg-[#FBEBCB] text-[#7A5410]',
  reject: 'bg-[#FBE3E0] text-[#9E2A21]',
};

const inputClass = 'mt-1.5 min-h-[48px] w-full rounded-2xl border border-line bg-paper px-4 text-[16px] text-ink placeholder:text-ink-3 focus:outline-none focus:ring-2 focus:ring-ink/30';

/** The words under the verdict: saved for other parents, or shown to this parent only (R2). */
function SharedLine({ reply }: { reply: AuditReply }) {
  if (reply.saved && reply.repeat) {
    return <p className="mt-4 text-[14.5px] font-semibold leading-snug text-[#17643F]">✓ Another parent already checked this offer, so you got its saved verdict at once.</p>;
  }
  if (reply.saved) {
    const n = reply.sharedFromParents;
    return (
      <>
        <p className="mt-4 text-[14.5px] font-semibold leading-snug text-[#17643F]">✓ Added to the shared list. The next parent checking this offer gets this verdict instantly.</p>
        <p data-testid="audit-thanks" className="mt-2 rounded-2xl bg-[#E3F3EA] px-3.5 py-3 text-[14.5px] font-semibold leading-snug text-[#17643F]">
          Thanks. You’re helping other parents{typeof n === 'number' ? `: ${n} offer${n === 1 ? '' : 's'} on the shared list came from parents.` : '.'}
        </p>
      </>
    );
  }
  return <p className="mt-4 text-[14.5px] font-semibold leading-snug text-ink-2">Shown to you only; not added to the shared list.</p>;
}

function Verdict({ reply, store, offer }: { reply: AuditReply; store: string; offer: string }) {
  return (
    <section role="status" aria-live="polite" aria-label="Verdict" className="mt-5 rounded-2xl border border-line bg-paper p-4" data-testid="audit-verdict">
      <p className="eyebrow text-ink-2">Verdict</p>
      <p className="mt-2"><span className={cn('inline-flex rounded-full px-3 py-1 text-[15px] font-extrabold', pill[reply.verdict])}>{verdictLabel[reply.verdict]}</span></p>
      <p className="mt-3 text-[17px] font-extrabold leading-snug text-ink">{store}’s “{offer}”</p>
      <p className="mt-1 text-[15px] leading-relaxed text-ink-2">{reply.summary}</p>
      {reply.hunter && (
        <div className="mt-3 rounded-xl bg-cream p-3">
          <p className="eyebrow text-[#17643F]">Deal Hunter</p>
          <p className="mt-1 text-[14.5px] leading-snug text-ink">{reply.hunter}</p>
        </div>
      )}
      {reply.lawyer && (
        <div className="mt-2 rounded-xl bg-cream p-3">
          <p className="eyebrow text-coral-deep">Fine-Print Lawyer</p>
          <p className="mt-1 text-[14.5px] leading-snug text-ink">{reply.lawyer}</p>
        </div>
      )}
      <SharedLine reply={reply} />
      {reply.mode === 'quick' && !reply.injection && (
        <p className="mt-3 rounded-xl bg-cream px-3 py-2.5 text-[13.5px] leading-snug text-ink-2">Quick check. The full AI review runs in live mode.</p>
      )}
    </section>
  );
}

/**
 * "Audit a deal": who is offering it, what you get, an optional link, and the fine print as pasted text or a screenshot.
 * The verdict names the store you typed. Nothing is invented on this screen: it shows what the server's court answered.
 */
export default function AuditDeal({ onBack, onSaved }: { onBack: () => void; onSaved?: () => void }) {
  useFreezeSpot();
  const ids = { store: useId(), offer: useId(), link: useId(), text: useId(), file: useId() };
  const [store, setStore] = useState('');
  const [offer, setOffer] = useState('');
  const [link, setLink] = useState('');
  const [source, setSource] = useState<Source>('paste');
  const [text, setText] = useState('');
  const [file, setFile] = useState<File | null>(null);
  const [fileProblem, setFileProblem] = useState<string | null>(null);
  const [phase, setPhase] = useState<Phase>({ kind: 'form' });
  const fileRef = useRef<HTMLInputElement>(null);

  const ready = store.trim() && offer.trim() && (source === 'paste' ? text.trim() : file) && phase.kind !== 'sending';

  const pick = (e: ChangeEvent<HTMLInputElement>) => {
    const f = e.target.files?.[0] ?? null;
    const bad = f ? checkPickedFile(f) : null;
    setFileProblem(bad); setFile(bad ? null : f);
  };

  const submit = async () => {
    setPhase({ kind: 'sending' });
    try {
      const base = { store: store.trim(), offer: offer.trim(), ...(link.trim() ? { link: link.trim() } : {}) };
      const body = source === 'paste'
        ? { ...base, text: text.trim() }
        : { ...base, ...(await preparePhoto(file as File)) };
      const reply = await sendAudit(body);
      setPhase({ kind: 'done', reply, store: base.store, offer: base.offer });
      if (reply.saved && !reply.repeat) onSaved?.();
    } catch (e) {
      setPhase({ kind: 'problem', message: e instanceof Error ? e.message : 'We could not check that deal just now. Please try again.' });
    }
  };

  const tab = (id: Source, label: string) => (
    <button
      type="button" role="tab" aria-selected={source === id} onClick={() => setSource(id)}
      className={cn('min-h-[44px] flex-1 rounded-xl px-3 text-[15px] font-bold', source === id ? 'bg-paper text-ink shadow-sm' : 'text-ink-2')}
    >{label}</button>
  );

  return (
    <section aria-label="Audit a deal" className="mt-4" data-testid="audit-deal">
      <button type="button" onClick={onBack} className="inline-flex min-h-[44px] items-center gap-1 text-[15px] font-bold text-ink">
        <span aria-hidden="true">‹</span> Back
      </button>
      <h1 className="mt-1 text-[30px] font-extrabold leading-[1.1] tracking-[-0.03em]">Audit a deal</h1>
      <p className="mt-2 text-[16px] leading-relaxed text-ink-2">Tell us about the offer. We’ll read the fine print for hidden catches. When our checks agree, the verdict goes on a shared list for other parents.</p>

      <form className="mt-4 space-y-4" onSubmit={(e) => { e.preventDefault(); if (ready) void submit(); }}>
        <div>
          <label htmlFor={ids.store} className="text-[15px] font-extrabold text-ink">Who’s offering it?</label>
          <input id={ids.store} className={inputClass} value={store} maxLength={80} onChange={(e) => setStore(e.target.value)} placeholder="Store or brand" autoComplete="off" />
        </div>
        <div>
          <label htmlFor={ids.offer} className="text-[15px] font-extrabold text-ink">What do you get?</label>
          <input id={ids.offer} className={inputClass} value={offer} maxLength={200} onChange={(e) => setOffer(e.target.value)} placeholder="For example: a free welcome box" autoComplete="off" />
        </div>
        <div>
          <label htmlFor={ids.link} className="text-[15px] font-extrabold text-ink">Link <span className="font-medium text-ink-2">(optional)</span></label>
          <input id={ids.link} type="url" inputMode="url" className={inputClass} value={link} maxLength={300} onChange={(e) => setLink(e.target.value)} placeholder="https://" autoComplete="off" />
        </div>
        <div>
          <p className="text-[15px] font-extrabold text-ink" id={`${ids.text}-h`}>Fine print</p>
          <div role="tablist" aria-labelledby={`${ids.text}-h`} className="mt-1.5 flex gap-1 rounded-2xl bg-[#F1ECE4] p-1">
            {tab('paste', 'Paste the text')}
            {tab('screenshot', 'Add a screenshot')}
          </div>
          {source === 'paste' ? (
            <textarea
              aria-label="Fine print" rows={5} value={text} maxLength={8000} onChange={(e) => setText(e.target.value)}
              placeholder="Paste the terms exactly as the offer shows them."
              className="mt-2 w-full rounded-2xl border border-line bg-paper px-4 py-3 text-[16px] leading-snug text-ink placeholder:text-ink-3 focus:outline-none focus:ring-2 focus:ring-ink/30"
            />
          ) : (
            <div className="mt-2">
              <label htmlFor={ids.file} className="text-[14px] font-semibold text-ink-2">Add a screenshot of the fine print</label>
              <input
                ref={fileRef} id={ids.file} type="file" accept="image/*" onChange={pick}
                className="mt-1.5 block w-full text-[15px] text-ink file:mr-3 file:min-h-[44px] file:rounded-xl file:border file:border-line file:bg-paper file:px-4 file:font-bold file:text-ink"
              />
              {file && <p className="mt-1 text-[13.5px] text-ink-2">Chosen: {file.name}</p>}
              {fileProblem && <p className="mt-1 text-[14px] font-semibold text-[#9E2A21]">{fileProblem}</p>}

          )}
        </div>
        <button
          type="submit" disabled={!ready}
          className="inline-flex min-h-[52px] w-full items-center justify-center rounded-2xl bg-ink px-4 text-[16px] font-extrabold text-cream disabled:opacity-40"
        >
          {phase.kind === 'sending' ? 'Reading the fine print…' : 'Check this deal'}

import type { ReactNode } from 'react';

interface Props {
  card: FeedCard;

  today?: string;

  pinned?: boolean;
  /** Where "How we checked" goes. Omit to hide the link (e.g. on the detail page itself). */

  /** A plain "Source" link (the card's own source page), shown where "How we checked" would be. Used for benefit cards. */
  sourceHref?: string;
  /** Shows "I got this" and "Not relevant" buttons. Leave out for cards a parent cannot act on (safety checks, coming-soon tiles). */
  actions?: { onGotIt: () => void; onNotRelevant: () => void };
  /** Replaces the deadline countdown (e.g. "Starts at birth" for an expecting family). */
  deadlineLabel?: string;
  /** Extra content shown under the card's sentence (e.g. the insurance deadline pill). */
  extra?: ReactNode;
}

function ExternalIcon() {
  return (
    <svg aria-hidden="true" viewBox="0 0 24 24" width="12" height="12" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" strokeWidth="2.2" strokeLinecap="round" strokeLinejoin="round">
      <path d="M14 4h6v6" /><path d="M20 4 10 14" /><path d="M19 14v5a1 1 0 0 1-1 1H5a1 1 0 0 1-1-1V6a1 1 0 0 1 1-1h5" />
    </svg>
  );
}

  all_clear: 'bg-[#E3F3EA] text-[#17643F]',

  blocked: 'bg-[#FBE3E0] text-[#9E2A21]',
};

  const meta = KIND_META[card.kind];
  const caption = amountCaption(card);
  const soon = card.kind === 'coming_soon';
  const sources = safeSources(card.sources);
  const due = deadlineLabel ? { text: deadlineLabel, urgent: false } : card.deadline ? cardDeadline(card.kind, card.deadline, today) : null;
  const checkWithJob = isCheckWithJob(card);
  const minutes = card.kind === 'discount' ? undefined : minutesOf(card); // deals already say their effort in the Value and time lines
  // A deal graded by the Fine Print Court says what the court found (verdict, minutes, true value, the baby's age) instead of a sentence.
  const facts = card.kind === 'discount' ? card.offerFacts : undefined;

  // Coming-soon tiles already say "Coming soon" in the eyebrow, so drop the repeat from the body.

  const eyebrow = pinned ? 'Pinned · Deadline' : card.deadline && card.kind === 'benefit' ? 'Benefit · Deadline' : store || meta.label;

  return (

import type { FeedCard } from '@shared/bundle';
import type { TraceLine } from '@/lib/bundle';
import { Link } from 'wouter';
import { zetarisForCard, memoryForCard, blockedReason } from '@/lib/howWeChecked';

const plural = (n: number, one: string, many: string) => `${n} ${n === 1 ? one : many}`;

/** "Data sources checked (via Zetaris)": plain-English source chips for this card. Renders nothing when no query maps to the card. */
export function ZetarisSection({ card, lines }: { card: FeedCard; lines: TraceLine[] }) {
  const v = zetarisForCard(card, lines);
  if (!v) return null;
  return (
    <section className="mt-6" aria-labelledby="zetaris-title" data-testid="zetaris-section">
      <h3 id="zetaris-title" className="eyebrow text-ink-2">Data sources checked (via Zetaris)</h3>
      <div className="mt-2 rounded-2xl border border-line bg-paper p-4">
        <ul className="flex flex-wrap gap-2" aria-label="Sources">
          {v.sources.map((s) => (
            <li key={s} className="rounded-full bg-coral-tint px-3 py-1 text-[13px] font-semibold leading-snug text-coral-deep">{s}</li>
          ))}
        </ul>
        <p className="mt-3 text-[14px] leading-relaxed text-ink-2" data-testid="zetaris-summary">
          {plural(v.queries, 'query', 'queries')} across {plural(v.sources.length, 'source', 'sources')}
          {v.saved ? ' · saved real response' : v.ms !== null ? ` · ${v.ms} ms` : ''}
        </p>
        <details className="mt-2">
          <summary className="min-h-[44px] cursor-pointer py-2 text-[14px] font-bold text-ink">Show query</summary>
          <p className="text-[12.5px] text-ink-2">Values are hidden for privacy.</p>
          {v.sql.map((q, i) => (
            <pre key={i} className="mt-2 whitespace-pre-wrap break-words rounded-xl bg-cream p-3 font-mono text-[11.5px] leading-relaxed text-ink">{q}</pre>
          ))}
        </details>
      </div>
    </section>
  );
}

/** "Memory (Meterless H-MEM)": learned rules recalled for this card's offer. Renders nothing when there are none. */
export function MemorySection({ card, lines }: { card: FeedCard; lines: TraceLine[] }) {
  const rules = memoryForCard(card, lines);
  if (rules.length === 0) return null;
  return (
    <section className="mt-6" aria-labelledby="memory-title" data-testid="memory-section">
      <h3 id="memory-title" className="eyebrow text-ink-2">Memory (Meterless H-MEM)</h3>
      <ul className="mt-2 space-y-2">
        {rules.map((r) => (
          <li key={r.id} className="rounded-2xl border border-line bg-paper p-4">
            <p className="text-[15px] font-bold leading-snug text-ink">{r.text}</p>
            <div className="mt-2 flex flex-wrap gap-2 text-[12.5px] font-semibold">
              <span className="rounded-full bg-cream px-2.5 py-1 font-mono text-ink">{r.id}</span>
              <span className="rounded-full bg-cream px-2.5 py-1 text-ink-2">confidence {Math.round(r.confidence * 100)}%</span>
              <span className="rounded-full bg-cream px-2.5 py-1 text-ink-2">learned from {plural(r.reports, 'parent report', 'parent reports')}</span>
              {r.cited && <span className="rounded-full bg-coral-tint px-2.5 py-1 text-coral-deep">cited by the Judge</span>}
            </div>
          </li>
        ))}
      </ul>
    </section>
  );
}

/** Collapsed "We caught these for you": offers the Fine Print Court rejected, with the learned rule it cited. Renders nothing when there are none. */
export function CaughtForYou({ blocked, lines, href }: { blocked: FeedCard[]; lines: TraceLine[]; href: (id: string) => string }) {
  if (blocked.length === 0) return null;
  return (
    <section className="mt-7" aria-label="We caught these for you" data-testid="caught-section">
      <details className="rounded-2xl border border-line bg-paper px-4">
        <summary className="flex min-h-[56px] cursor-pointer items-center justify-between gap-3 text-[16px] font-bold text-ink">
          <span>We caught these for you</span>
          <span className="rounded-full bg-[#FBE3E0] px-2.5 py-0.5 text-[13px] font-bold text-[#9E2A21]">{blocked.length}</span>
        </summary>
        <p className="text-[14px] text-ink-2">Offers we blocked because of their fine print. They are not counted in your totals.</p>
        <ul className="mt-2 space-y-3 pb-4">
          {blocked.map((c) => (
            <li key={c.id} className="rounded-2xl border border-line bg-cream p-3">
              <Link href={href(c.id)} className="block min-h-[44px]">
                <span className="block text-[15px] font-bold leading-snug text-ink">{c.title}</span>
                <span className="mt-1 block text-[14px] leading-relaxed text-ink-2">{blockedReason(c)}</span>
                <span className="mt-1 block text-[13px] font-bold text-coral-deep">See how we checked ›</span>
              </Link>
              <MemorySection card={c} lines={lines} />
            </li>
          ))}
        </ul>
      </details>
    </section>
  );
}
